correctness.rationale: PASS: Adjacent absolute differences in {1,…,n−1} are encoded injectively in n−1 four-bit digits for n≤10. Lexicographic permutation enumeration visits each permutation once, counts every realized fiber, and gives exact maxima (2,2,6,4,8,8,30,12,24), maximizing counts (1,3,1,6,3,5,1,20,5). Independent newly authored C++ exhaustive census for all 2≤n≤10 checked Σfiber=n!, 1,528,045 distinct n=10 records, unique n=8 (4,2,4,1,4,2,4) with 30 solutions; independent signed-increment DFS and reversal/complementation orbit partition gave seven size-4 and one size-2 orbits. Finite completeness follows from exhaustive finite enumeration, not extrapolation to n>10.

value.rationale: PASS: Exact worst-case ambiguity of a natural information-losing permutation measurement is a meaningful finite classification and reconstructability benchmark. The surprising fall from 30 at n=8 to 12 at n=9, recovery to 24 at n=10, and explicit unique n=8 extremal orbit structure are nontrivial sharp finite cutoffs, not arbitrary sample averages. Full finite enumeration is a rigorous finite proof.

limitations: Only n=2..10; no all-n extrapolation or complexity claim.
Counts permutations distinctly even when reversal/complementation symmetry relates them.
